depth_justification: The first turn and final report engage PainTrack's actual features (body-map annotations, PDF-to-clinic, FHIR/EHR, patient-controlled sharing) with precise and largely correct GDPR cites (Art. 9(2)(h) for confidentiality-bound clinicians, 7(3) bundled-consent withdrawal, 44-49 transfers), but the identical [P2.D8] data-sharing block is repeated verbatim across five turns with no progression, and it conflates 'AI classification' with GDPR Art. 35 instead of the EU AI Act.
actionability_justification: Gives concrete, implementable moves with the exact lawful-basis articles and artifacts (explicit granular per-purpose opt-in consent with easy withdrawal and an audit log; Art. 9(2)(h) for clinician sharing; SCCs/BCRs/adequacy for Art. 44-49 transfers; encryption + integrity checks), though a few items stay directional ('conduct a risk assessment', 'ensure data minimization').
salient_examples: Implement explicit, granular, per-purpose opt-in consent for data sharing with clinicians, with easy withdrawal and an audit log ... GDPR Article 9(2)(a) and 6(1)(a)
justified under GDPR Article 9(2)(h) (care provided by a confidentiality-bound professional) (precise, apt cite)
Identical [P2.D8] data-sharing block repeated verbatim across 5 consecutive ASSISTANT turns
classification of the AI system under Article 35 of the GDPR (conflates DPIA with AI Act classification)
